scope: Selected AFTA rows 16, 17 and 19, FDP_ACF.1.1/1.2/1.4: token IP attribute source and allow/deny enforcement only

baseline_regression.interpretation: A client-supplied X-Forwarded-For satisfied a token IP rule despite a disallowed remote address; another raw header wrongly rejected an allowed servlet address. Servlet-filter reproduction with mocked token/account authentication, not evidence of exploitation in a deployed network.

implementation.address_source: HttpServletRequest.getRemoteAddr(), not a raw X-Forwarded-For header
implementation.proxy_contract: Any client-address rewriting must be performed by a container/proxy integration that validates trusted proxy peers and sanitizes forwarding headers; application code does not establish that deployment trust.
implementation.compatibility: IP-constrained tokens behind a proxy can be denied until trusted servlet address resolution is configured. Adding a shared proxy IP allows all clients arriving through that proxy. Tokens without IP constraints retain existing behavior.
implementation.other_rules: Method/referrer rules and owner/token validation remain; method-denial interaction tested

conditions.test_boundary: Real servlet filter, API-token resolver/checksum/hash and security-context handling; mocked token/account manager, failure entry point, event publisher and filter chain. No external HTTP requests.
conditions.dependencies: Offline existing Maven cache, retaining the unchanged sms-compression 0.3.2 source-build caveat from afta-token-owner-binding-2026-11-12.json.
